title: An algebraic group scheme over a field is quasi-projective

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: reduce to the connected component over an algebraically closed field; in characteristic zero G is smooth and in characteristic p the reduction H is a smooth group scheme, so it suffices to treat a quasi-compact irreducible smooth group scheme over an algebraically closed field; choose an etale cover U of G over an affine space, a finite etale refinement W -> V, build the effective Cartier divisor T = (1 x pi')(D) on G x V whose components are Cartier since G x V has UFD local rings, and show the fibres E_v are unions of translates of D with affine complements avoiding any given k-point; the resulting invertible sheaves O_G(E_v) have constant class L by the rational-equivalence lemma, and the canonical sections give nonvanishing sections with affine nonvanishing loci, so L is ample by definition (source lines 1587-1697)

core_obligations: Reduction (proof lines 1588-1615): after passing to k-bar (0BDC) every component of G is a translate of G^0 (0B7R), there are finitely many because G is quasi-compact Noetherian, so it suffices to treat a connected G; in characteristic zero G is smooth (047N) and in characteristic p the reduction H = G_red is a smooth group scheme (047R, 047P), and an ample sheaf on H pushes the question back via 0BD4.

Divisor machinery (proof lines 1616-1660): the local rings of a smooth irreducible G are regular hence UFD (056S, 0AG0); the complement of a nonempty affine open is the support of an effective Cartier divisor D (0BCW, G separated by 047L); choose an etale U -> A^d_k (054L) with finite etale refinement pi': W -> V of degree n, form T = (1 x pi')(D) on G x V, note its components have codimension 1 in the smooth scheme G x V and are therefore effective Cartier divisors (0AGA), giving the divisor E with sheaf M = O(E).

Ampleness (proof lines 1661-1678): for v in V(k) the fibre E_v is the union of the n translates D j(w_i)^{-1}, so G \\ E_v is affine (intersections of affine opens in the separated G); each g in G(k) avoids some E_v (choose v over which the open W' has all n points); the classes of O_G(E_v) are constant in Pic by 0BEH, so the canonical sections (01WX) give sections s_v of a single invertible sheaf L, nonvanishing at g with affine nonvanishing locus; this is ampleness by definition (01PS).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a smooth irreducible group scheme over an algebraically closed field (proof lines 1588-1615).
Build the Cartier divisor E on G x V from D via the finite etale refinement (proof lines 1616-1660).
Read the fibres E_v as a constant Picard class with sections avoiding every k-point and with affine nonvanishing loci; conclude ampleness by definition (proof lines 1661-1678).
